key_risks: Delayed claim settlements, lower reimbursement rates, and complex compliance requirements from insurance companies, corporates, and government schemes straining cash flows.
Stringent pricing negotiations by insurance providers and government health schemes leading to reduced margins compared to self-paying patients.
Availability and retention of qualified doctors, nurses, and healthcare professionals affected by constraints in medical education capacity, rising manpower costs, and talent migration.
Increasing competition from established hospital chains, diagnostic centers, and healthcare startups with continued capacity build-out through greenfield and brownfield expansion.
Relatively modest public health expenditure as a share of GDP and stagnant financing alongside rising burden of non-communicable diseases increasing pressure on private healthcare infrastructure.
Changing laws, rules, regulations, and legal uncertainties including adverse application of tax laws.
